title: Top Word Outside the Ban List
statement:
You get a piece of text text and a list of lowercase banned words. A word is a maximal run of English letters; every other character (spaces and the symbols !?',;.) separates words. Words are compared ignoring case.

Return, in lowercase, the word that appears most often in text and is not banned. The input guarantees that at least one word is not banned and that the answer is unique.

examples.in: text = "Rain, rain. Go away! Go home, RAIN?", banned = ["rain"]
examples.why: "rain" appears three times in different cases but is banned. "go" appears twice.
Commas and semicolons separate words even without spaces. "tab" appears 3 times, "space" twice.
The apostrophe is a separator, so "it's" is the two words "it" and "s".

constraints: text has English letters, spaces and the symbols !?',;.

args: Rain, rain. Go away! Go home, RAIN?
a b. B? c; C, c!
A, A  A. an, AN  A!An

hints: Split the text into words first. What should count as a separator?
Anything that is not a letter separates words. Lowercase every word as you collect it.
Count words in a hash map, skipping banned ones (put them in a set), and return the word with the highest count.

explain.intuition:
Two jobs: tokenize, then count. Tokenizing means walking the text and building a word while you see letters, finishing it at any other character. Counting is a hash map, with the banned words in a set so each check is O(1).

This is the same pipeline a search box uses before ranking: normalize case, split on punctuation, drop stop words, count.
steps: Walk the text, appending lowercase letters to the current word. At any non-letter (and at the end), finish the current word if it is non-empty.
For each finished word not in the banned set, increment its count.
Return the word with the largest count.
pitfalls: Splitting on spaces only. "tab,space" is two words, and "it's" is it + s.
Forgetting to flush the last word when the text ends with a letter.
Comparing case-sensitively, so Rain and rain are counted separately.

complexity.time: O(length of text + total length of banned)

solutions.title: Split on non-letters and count
solutions.idea: Lowercase, replace every non-letter with a space, split, and count allowed words.

solutions.title: Manual tokenizer
solutions.idea: Build words character by character, flushing at each separator, so there is no regex and one pass.

followups: Return the top k allowed words, ties broken alphabetically.
The text is a stream too large for memory, but the vocabulary is small. What changes?
